picks.why: Among the cheapest sound businesses on the sheet at 11.1x trailing with EPS still growing 10.1%; it is a top-tier auto insurer whose float reinvests near a 4.7% 10Y, and people keep buying car insurance whatever the consumer data or this week's retail prints say.
At 12.8x trailing with net cash, the Barrick settlement windfall and gold at $4,380, it is this book's hedge against the synthesis's stagflation tail, held rather than chased with RSI near 71.

A first-rate staple at 16.8x trailing after a 5.5% 12-week slide and only 2.1% weekly volatility; it fits the cheap-staple rotation the synthesis names as its hedge, and a WMT margin miss mainly threatens the 40x-plus defensives, not this one.

At 16.0x trailing on 43.9% EPS growth, and up only 4.7% over 12 weeks against JPM's 19%, it is the cheaper way into the synthesis's biggest opening: the confirmed XLF breakout, with Basel capital relief still unpriced.

A cheap compounder at 16.8x with an investment-grade balance sheet and no report until November, it is the consumer name the Council has me owning through the retail noise instead of renting a recovery trade.

summary: A quality-value book: two of the cheapest sound names on the sheet (PGR, NEM) plus fairly priced franchises (GS, PEP, DIS), split between the synthesis's biggest opening (the financials breakout) and its hedges (cheap staples, gold) against the stagflation tail and the Jackson Hole gate. I left out this week's reporters (DE, HD, WMT), REGN's binary decision, refiners trading above target, energy after a +7.67% week, trailing P/Es that look inflated by one-off gains (GOOGL, AMZN) and HON's P/E, which is muddied by its breakup. I have no memory of how this week went and used only these two files.
